extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners, patent owners, and patent practitioners handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for handling appeals, examiner answers, interviews, disclosure obligations, hearings, and multiple copending ex parte reexamination proceedings under the MPEP and cited CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal brief compliance with 37 CFR 41.37
rubrics_metrics.description: The brief must set forth the authorities and arguments relied on; mere filing of a paper entitled 'brief' does not guarantee compliance with 37 CFR 41.37.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the brief fails to set forth authorities/arguments with respect to any ground of rejection, that ground may be summarily sustained. Distinguish between (A) lack of any argument — summarily sustain the rejection, and (B) presentation of arguments that carry no conviction — decide on the merits (may still affirm). Appellant must traverse every ground of rejection set forth in the final rejection that is presented for review; oral argument will not remedy failure to traverse. Ignoring or acquiescing in any rejection invites summarily affirmance, even for formal matters curable by amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content and effect of Examiner's Answer (37 CFR 41.39)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner's answer is deemed to incorporate all grounds of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified), unless expressly withdrawn; it may include a new ground of rejection which must be designated as new and requires Director approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any rejection that relies upon evidence not relied upon in the Office action shall be designated a new ground of rejection. Examiner must obtain Director approval to furnish an answer that includes a new ground. Examiner's answer may expressly indicate withdrawal of a ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's response options to a new ground of rejection (37 CFR 41.39(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner's answer contains a new ground of rejection, appellant must within two months either (1) request reopening of prosecution or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief addressing the new ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (1) Reopen prosecution: file a reply under 37 CFR 1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits/evidence; amendments/affidavits must be relevant to the new ground and will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal. (2) Maintain appeal: file a reply brief under 37 CFR 41.41 addressing each new ground as set forth in 41.37(c)(1)(iv) and follow other brief requirements; a reply brief may not be accompanied by any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence — if accompanied, it is treated as a request to reopen prosecution. Extensions under 1.136(a) are not applicable to these periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental Examiner's Answer limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: After a timely reply brief or supplemental examiner's answer, the examiner may acknowledge receipt, reopen prosecution, or furnish a supplemental examiner's answer responding to new issues raised in the reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental examiner's answer responding to a reply brief may not include a new ground of rejection. A supplemental examiner's answer (other than to respond to new issues raised in the reply brief) is not permitted unless the reexamination proceeding has been remanded by the Board. See MPEP § 1207.05 for handling supplemental answers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request requirements (37 CFR 41.73/41.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain an oral hearing the appellant (patent owner) must file a written request and pay the fee within two months after the date of the examiner's answer or supplemental examiner's answer; the period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appellant may participate in an oral hearing unless the request and fee are timely filed. In reexamination proceedings hearings are open to the public as observers unless the appellant petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 to close the hearing, presents sufficient reasons, pays the petition fee, and the petition is granted. See MPEP § 1209 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal to courts and standing
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner dissatisfied with the Board's decision may seek judicial review to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 141; a third party requester of an ex parte reexamination may not seek judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory amendments and applicable effective dates determine exact appeal routes (see Public Law references in MPEP). Courts may permit intervention by a third party requester in appropriate circumstances, but intervention does not confer standing to appeal the court's decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure and candor in reexamination (37 CFR 1.555(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner (patent owner, attorneys/agents, and those substantively involved) has a continuing duty of candor and good faith to disclose all information known to be material to patentability in a reexamination proceeding for each pending claim until the claim is cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The duty is satisfied if all information known to be material to patentability of any claim after issuance of the reexamination certificate was cited by the Office or submitted in an IDS. Fraud, bad faith, or intentional misconduct in disclosure results in noncompliance. The Office will not itself evaluate compliance; unresolved questions will be noted under 1.552(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'information material to patentability' (37 CFR 1.555(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material when it is not cumulative and (1) is a patent or printed publication that establishes, alone or in combination, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) refutes or is inconsistent with a position the patent owner takes in opposing an unpatentability argument or asserting patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prima facie case is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under the preponderance of the evidence standard, giving each claim term the broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, and before considering evidence to establish a contrary conclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and form of Information Disclosure Statements in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An IDS should be filed with the items listed in 37 CFR 1.98(a) and should be filed within two months of the order for reexamination or as soon thereafter as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An IDS filed after the order and before the first action on the merits may be submitted as part of a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 (and may include discussion of patentability issues), or as a separate paper limited to listing the information and explaining relevance. If separate, any discussion relating to patentability issues is improper. Copies required by 1.98(a)(2) must be supplied; exception in 1.98(d) does not apply to reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document copy requirements (37 CFR 1.98(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties submitting documents cited in the patent or parent applications must supply legible copies: (1) each foreign patent, (2) each publication or the portion causing it to be listed (other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications unless required), (3) for each cited pending unpublished U.S. application, the application specification including claims and drawings or the portion causing it to be listed, (4) all other information or portion causing it to be listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1.98(d) exception does not apply to ex parte and inter partes reexamination proceedings because reexamination does not rely on the patent for an earlier effective filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing duty to report prior or concurrent proceedings (37 CFR 1.565)
rubrics_metrics.description: In ex parte reexamination, the patent owner must inform the Office of any prior or concurrent proceedings (interferences, reissues, reexaminations, litigation, PTAB reviews, supplemental examinations) in which the patent is or was involved and the results, if known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office will accept copies of notices of suits and decisions for the reexamination file, but submissions must be limited to notification and not include arguments. Non-merit procedural decisions will generally not be entered. If submissions are not limited to bare notice, they will be returned, expunged, or discarded. The Office may limit entries for voluminous materials; submitters should identify application/proceeding numbers and statuses rather than full copending files. Form paragraphs 22.07 and 22.08 may be used to remind patent owners of this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews in ex parte reexamination — who, where, when (37 CFR 1.560(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews between examiners and patent owners or their attorneys/agents must be conducted in the Office during office hours at designated times; interviews for patentability discussion will not be conducted prior to the first official action except in limited passive-amendment circumstances initiated by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews should be arranged in advance. Requests by third-party requesters to participate or attend will not be granted. Telephonic and videoconferencing interviews are permitted according to MPEP § 713.01 guidelines. Interviews for patentability discussion ordinarily occur after the first Office action following the order for reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent owner's written statement after interview (37 CFR 1.560(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For every interview in an ex parte reexamination where matters of substance are discussed, the patent owner must file a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action either as a separate paper within one month after the interview or as part of a response to an outstanding Office action, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file the written statement as required will result in termination of the reexamination prosecution (per 37 CFR 1.550(d)). The examiner must complete an Ex Parte Interview Summary form PTOL-474 for each interview where a matter of substance was discussed; a copy should be given to the patent owner if practicable, the original is made of record, and copies mailed to third-party requester and patent owner if not already provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview preparation, duration, and frequency limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent owner desires an interview, they should contact the examiner and, if granted, file at least three working days prior an informal written statement of issues and an informal copy of any proposed claims to be discussed (unless waived); interview duration will not exceed one hour absent petition showing good cause; only one interview may be requested after an Office action and prior to filing the response absent good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal copies should be faxed or hand-carried to the examiner to match with the file; these preliminary materials will be made of record as attachment to PTOL-474. Examiner may extend interview time at sole discretion. A second interview after final rejection requires advance showing that it will expedite appeal/disposal. Panel members who conducted panel review will be present if practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on discussions with non-patent owners (procedural vs merits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners may discuss only strictly procedural matters with parties who are not the patent owner; matters that can be obtained by reading the public file are procedural and may be discussed to the extent shown in the file, while matters not available in the file are considered merits and may not be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (A) information obtainable from reading the file is procedural; (B) matters not in the file are merits and may not be discussed. Questions regarding interpretation of claim limitations are merits — examiner may only quote the Office action and not further discuss. Parties not the patent owner should be referred to CRU SPRS or TC QAS for procedural questions beyond the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch and interview pre-submission requirements (35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to statutory 'special dispatch' in reexamination proceedings, preliminary steps are required to structure interviews for efficiency: patent owner should contact examiner to indicate issues and, if interview is granted, submit informal written statement and copies of proposed claims at least three working days prior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These materials should be transmitted directly to the examiner (fax or hand-carried) to avoid delays; informal copies considered by the examiner will become part of the record attached to the PTOL-474. The one-hour guideline is based on the expectation that claims in a reexamined patent will already define the invention sufficiently; extensions require petition showing sufficient cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple copending ex parte reexamination proceedings and merger (37 CFR 1.565/§ 2240 linkage)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ex parte reexamination is ordered while a prior ex parte reexamination is pending and prosecution in the prior proceeding has not been terminated, the proceedings will usually be merged and result in issuance/publication of a single certificate; the CRU Director decides whether to combine proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a second or subsequent ex parte request to be granted, the later request must raise a substantial new question of patentability based on the patents/printed publications cited in that request. No decision on combining should be made until reexamination is actually ordered in the later-filed request. See MPEP § 2240 and § 2686.01 for inter partes/merger specifics.
